output.title: CQRS with event sourcing
output.description: Commands append events to an event store; projections build read models that queries hit, and an outbound feed shares events.

simulations.title: Payday: reads outnumber writes
simulations.description: 400 commands and 1,600 queries; writes and reads scale independently.

action.text: Payday. Commands go to the write side; queries never touch it. Each dot is five requests.
The event store is the source of truth: an append-only log of what happened. Each projection keeps its own position in it.
Queries read denormalized tables, so reads stay fast however long an account's history grows.

simulations.title: Rebuild a read model
simulations.description: A new statement projection replays 2,000 historical events while live traffic continues.

action.text: Statements need a new field. Instead of migrating the index, we deploy a new projection and rebuild it from the log.
The old projection stops. New events wait in its subscription; balances and the public feed are unaffected.
Version 2 replays 2,000 historical events from position zero, then picks up the live ones. Statements are briefly stale; nothing is lost.

expectations.label: Statements fall behind during the rebuild
History and live events are indexed
